passages.original: cognito repente insperato gaudio expirasse animam refert Aristoteles philosophus Polycritam, nobilem feminam Naxo insula.
passages.english: The philosopher Aristotle relates that Polycrita, a noble woman from the island of Naxos, breathed out her life when a sudden, unhoped-for joy became known to her.

passages.original: EURIPIDI poetae matrem Theopompus agrestia olera vendentem victum quaesisse dicit.
passages.english: Theopompus says that the mother of the poet Euripides earned her living by selling wild vegetables.
passages.notes: 'Agrestia olera' may mean either 'wild' or 'country/field' vegetables, i.e. greens gathered or grown in the countryside.

passages.original: Set elleborum sumi posse tutissime in insula Anticyra Plinius Secundus in libris Naturalis Historiae scripsit. Propterea Livium Drusum, qui tribunus plebi fuit, cum morbum qui comitialis dicitur pateretur, Anticyram navigasse et in ea insula elleborum bibisse ait, atque ita inorbo liberatum.
passages.english: But Plinius Secundus wrote in the books of his Natural History that hellebore can be taken most safely on the island of Anticyra. For this reason, he says, Livius Drusus, who was tribune of the plebs, since he suffered from the disease that is called 'comitial', sailed to Anticyra and drank hellebore on that island, and so was freed from the disease.
passages.notes: 'Comitial disease' (morbus comitialis) is epilepsy, so called because an attack was held to break up an assembly (comitia). 'inorbo' is a scanning error for 'morbo'.
